For normalized HSTU embeddings, define logits as s(u,i)=cos(hᵤ,eᵢ)/τ; apply sampling corrections after temperature scaling. Exclude padding, the target, and every known training positive from each user’s negative pool, using training data only. Rejection sampling changes the proposal to qᵤ(i)=q(i)/Σeligible q(j); corrections must reflect that conditional distribution. Excluding historical positives defines a restricted-catalog objective, rather than approximating unrestricted full-catalog softmax. TensorFlow documents target-collision removal, but excluding all user positives requires additional per-user handling. [Sampled-softmax documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/sampled_softmax_loss).

A concrete importance-sampled objective with the positive included exactly once is L=−s(u,y)+log[exp(s(u,y))+(1/K)Σₖ exp(s(u,nₖ))/qᵤ(nₖ)], for K independent draws with replacement. Thus leave the positive logit unchanged and subtract log(Kqᵤ(nₖ)) from negative logits. Duplicate draws are valid multiplicities; collapsing them requires retaining their counts. If sampling a unique set instead, weight each negative by its inclusion probability πᵤ(i), using s−log πᵤ(i). These are estimator-derived prescriptions: do not deduplicate while retaining replacement-based corrections. TensorFlow’s conventional sampled-softmax formulation instead corrects both true and sampled logits using sampler expected counts; that is a distinct convention, not interchangeable with this deterministic-positive estimator. [Sampling definitions](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf), [sampler semantics](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/random/log_uniform_candidate_sampler).

Uncorrected sampled cross-entropy directly applies CE to the positive and sampled negatives. It optimizes discrimination against the chosen sampler; sampler frequency, duplicate multiplicity, and negative count affect the objective. Corrected sampled softmax targets a catalog-normalizer approximation, but finite-sample loss/gradients generally remain biased. Name and specify the exact variant. [Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.00527).
